input.message:
UPDATE: PR #70 merged — added Miles clarity fix on top of the SEO changes.

Community was confused about Miles ("How can 60k volume = 0 Miles?"). The /learn articles said "every swap earns Miles" which isn't accurate — Miles are only earned when swaps generate extractable mev.

Fixed language across 4 articles (miles.mdx, mev-rewards.mdx, what-are-fast-swaps.mdx, what-is-fast-protocol.mdx):
• Removed all "every swap earns Miles" claims
• Added explicit callout: volume alone does not guarantee Miles — stablecoin swaps in deep liquidity during calm markets can generate zero mev and therefore zero Miles
• Updated the airline analogy to reflect that not every trip earns the same
• FAQ answers updated with the same caveats

This should give Abdel and the community team clear language to point users to when the question comes up.

3. What makes preconfirmation *feel* different from regular tx confirmation? How to convey the speed advantage viscerally?
4. Any examples of apps that use branded animations for transaction milestones?
5. What's the psychology behind making sub-second confirmations feel impactful vs. "did anything happen?"

Compile findings into actionable UX recommendations for our notification system. The preconfirmed state should invoke joy/dopamine/celebration, while the tokens-available state should be a subtle wallet balance update animation.

Move primary experience from floating toasts to an inline status bar within the swap widget. The speed number is the viral hook -- design everything to make it prominent, shareable, and impossible to miss.
**Rationale:** (1) No competitor can replicate this because no competitor has preconfirmations. (2) The elapsed timer + frozen speed number creates a natural word-of-mouth loop. (3) Inline placement ensures 100% visibility vs corner toasts users may miss. (4) Zero new dependencies -- CSS keyframes + transforms only. (5) Directly supports investor demo narrative and staged rollout (users will screenshot and share organically).
**Risk:** (1) Over-animation could feel gimmicky -- mitigated by Phase 1 shipping clean/minimal version first. (2) Timer showing slow times on bad days could backfire -- mitigated by only showing timer when preconfirmation is sub-2s. (3) Inline bar takes space in the swap widget -- mitigated by it only appearing during active swaps and auto-dismissing.

input.message:
*Fast Swap: sign-to-preconfirmed speed optimizations* (`preconf-exp` branch)

Found and fixed several latency bottlenecks in the swap flow:

*ERC-20 swaps were routing through an unnecessary Vercel serverless proxy.* The `/api/fastswap` route was a pure pass-through — no auth, no secrets, no transformation — just forwarding to `fastrpc.mev-commit.xyz/fastswap`. Every ERC-20 swap paid a 100-300ms tax for the serverless cold start + extra network hop. FastRPC has `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so the browser can call it directly. Removed the proxy from the swap path.

Other optimizations:
• Removed a redundant `getFreshGasFees()` call before wallet popup on ETH path — fetched a block for baseFee but the result was never used. Wallet handles gas pricing. Saves 200-500ms.
• Removed duplicate polling — `useSwapConfirmation` and `SwapToast` were both running independent `useWaitForTxConfirmation` for the same hash (4 redundant API calls/sec → 2).
• Adaptive polling — first 5 polls at 100ms instead of fixed 500ms. Catches sub-second preconfirmations without the 250ms average detection delay.
• Pre-warmed tx-timeout config on page load instead of first poll.
• Abort signal propagation — parent cancel now kills in-flight fetches immediately.

Also shipped preconfirmation notification UX: celebration animation, "Preconfirmed in X.Xs" speed timer, level-up sound, share on X, auto-dismissing confirmed state with green checkmark badge, clickable max balance.

Preview: https://fastprotocolapp-git-preconf-exp-primev-da84fd63.vercel.app

The mctransactions DB lags ~15s behind the actual preconfirmation.
Now polls FastRPC's mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments JSON-RPC
in parallel — the node knows about commitments instantly since it
received them directly from the provider.

Three sources now race in parallel:
1. mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments (fastest — node has it)
2. eth_getTransactionReceipt via FastRPC
3. mctransactions DB (slowest, kept as fallback)

Note: ideal solution is eth_sendRawTransactionSync which returns
the commitment in the same call, but requires backend changes to
the /fastswap relayer endpoint for the Permit path.

EOF

*FastRPC `/fastswap` endpoint latency — team should investigate*

Instrumented the ERC-20 swap pipeline on the frontend and found the latency breakdown:

```
Toast created (placeholder hash)     t=0ms
  │
  │  fetch(fastrpc.mev-commit.xyz/fastswap)
  │  ← 2,207ms round trip
  │
Hash arrives, polling starts         t=2,207ms
  │
  │  Polling mctransactions DB + eth_getTransactionReceipt
  │  Both only return results after L1 block inclusion
  │  ← 15,205ms
  │
"Preconfirmed" detected              t=17,412ms
```

Two issues:

*1. `/fastswap` takes 2.2s to respond.* Network latency to FastRPC is only ~150ms (tested `eth_blockNumber`). The 2.2s is the relayer doing work — receiving the intent, routing through Barter, constructing the tx, broadcasting. Can this be optimized? Specifically: can the txHash be returned earlier (before full execution) so the frontend can start polling sooner? Or can Barter routing be cached/pre-warmed?

*2. The frontend was detecting "preconfirmed" via L1 block inclusion, not the actual commitment.* The `mctransactions` DB and `eth_getTransactionReceipt` both only update after L1 inclusion (~12s block + indexing). We've now added `mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments` as a polling source which should detect the commitment from the FastRPC node directly. Testing now.

Ideal fix: `/fastswap` should use `eth_sendRawTransactionSync` internally and return the commitment data in the response. That way the frontend gets txHash + preconfirmed in one shot — zero polling needed. The response could include a `commitments` field alongside `txHash`.

Branch: `preconf-exp` — preview: https://fastprotocolapp-git-preconf-exp-primev-da84fd63.vercel.app

input.message:
*Follow-up: `/fastswap` relayer likely bypasses the mev-commit commitment pipeline*

Correction on previous post — commitments should exist regardless of which builder wins the block. The commitment is made by the provider at bid time on the mev-commit network, not at block inclusion.

So the fact that `mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments` returns `"failed to get transaction commitments"` for Permit path (ERC-20) swaps means the `/fastswap` relayer is probably broadcasting the tx directly to Ethereum without going through FastRPC's `eth_sendRawTransaction` pipeline — so no bid is placed on mev-commit, no provider responds with a commitment, and no preconfirmation happens.

Evidence:
- **ETH path** (wallet sends through FastRPC RPC → `eth_sendRawTransaction`): commitment found in 570ms
- **Permit path** (`/fastswap` relayer submits internally): `"failed to get transaction commitments"` on every poll for 10s, falls back to L1 inclusion

The relayer needs to route its tx through the same `eth_sendRawTransaction` (or `eth_sendRawTransactionSync`) flow so the tx enters the mev-commit bid/commitment cycle. Without this, ERC-20 swaps via the Permit path are not actually getting preconfirmed — they're just getting normal L1 confirmations.

- **Preconfirmation celebration**: particle burst animation, spring-bounce Fast logo, level-up sound (C5-E5-G5 arpeggio), "Preconfirmed in X.Xs" speed badge
- **Single evolving toast card**: pending → preconfirmed (blue, particles, speed timer) → confirmed (green checkmark badge on Fast logo, auto-dismiss 6s with progress bar)
- **Share on X**: flush strip below card with natural tweet variations mentioning Ethereum mainnet + @Fast_Protocol/@ethereum/@ethereumfdn. Dynamic OG image card via edge-rendered `/api/og/preconfirm`
- **17.4s → 0.6s preconfirmation detection** (ETH path): added `mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments` as fastest polling source — queries FastRPC node directly instead of waiting for mctransactions DB (~15s L1 inclusion lag)
- **Eliminated Vercel serverless proxy** for ERC-20 swaps: `/api/fastswap` was a pure pass-through, FastRPC CORS allows direct client calls
- **Removed redundant `getFreshGasFees()`** before wallet popup (result was unused, saved 200-500ms)
- **Removed duplicate polling**: `useSwapConfirmation` + `SwapToast` both ran independent polling for the same hash
- **Adaptive polling**: 100ms initial (catches sub-second preconfs) → 500ms backoff
- **Pre-warmed tx-timeout config** on page load
- **Clickable balance** fills max amount (reserves 0.01 ETH gas for native ETH)
- **Removed `eth.merkle.io` fallback** in wagmi transports (no CORS, ~40 console errors/session)
- **Clear error on gas estimation revert** instead of raw viem dump
- **Standardized "preconfirmed"** (no hyphen) across all UI code
- **Cleaned all debug console.logs**

## Gating integrity

Zero changes to whitelisting/gating files. Verified:
- `SwapOrLandingGate.tsx` — untouched
- `use-gate-status.ts` — untouched  
- `middleware.ts` — untouched
- `/api/gate/*`, `/api/whitelist/*` — untouched
- `use-whitelist.ts`, `gate-data.ts` — untouched

All changes are inside the swap execution path (post-gate).

## Known issue

ERC-20 Permit path swaps don't get actual preconfirmations — the `/fastswap` relayer appears to bypass FastRPC's commitment pipeline. `mevcommit_getTransactionCommitments` returns errors for relayer-submitted txs. Posted to #claws for backend team investigation.

- [ ] ETH → token swap: verify celebration animation, speed timer, sound, share on X
- [ ] Token → token swap (Permit path): verify toast flow works (preconf detection depends on backend fix)
- [ ] Click balance on sell card: fills max with 0.01 ETH gas reserve
- [ ] Click balance on buy card: fills amount
- [ ] Verify whitelisting still blocks non-approved wallets
- [ ] Check console for errors — eth.merkle.io spam should be gone
- [ ] Test share on X tweet text + OG card rendering on production domain

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server"

/**
 * Returns raw HTML with OG/Twitter meta tags for share card rendering.
 * Twitter's crawler doesn't execute JS, so we can't use generateMetadata.
 * Human visitors get redirected to / via meta refresh.
 */
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const raw = parseFloat(request.nextUrl.searchParams.get("time") || "0.4")
  const time = !isNaN(raw) && raw >= 0 && raw <= 999 ? raw.toFixed(1) : "0.4"

  const title = `Preconfirmed in ${time}s — Fast Swaps`
  const description = `Swap preconfirmed in ${time} seconds on Fast Protocol`
  const origin = request.nextUrl.origin
  const ogImage = `${origin}/api/og/preconfirm?time=${time}`

  const html = `<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <title>${title}</title>
  <meta name="description" content="${description}" />
  <meta property="og:title" content="${title}" />
  <meta property="og:description" content="${description}" />
  <meta property="og:image" content="${ogImage}" />
  <meta property="og:image:width" content="1200" />
  <meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />
  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
  <meta name="twitter:site" content="@Fast_Protocol" />
  <meta name="twitter:title" content="${title}" />
  <meta name="twitter:description" content="${description}" />
  <meta name="twitter:image" content="${ogImage}" />
  <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=/" />
</head>
<body></body>
</html>`

  return new NextResponse(html, {
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "text/html; charset=utf-8",
      "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=3600",
    },
  })
}
